title: Best Book Cover Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a book cover designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: Readers judge a book by its cover, usually as a small thumbnail in an online store. A good cover tells them the genre at a glance and still reads clearly when tiny. Covers go wrong when the image rights are unclear or the print file does not match the final page count. This guide covers both.

faq.q: Do I need an ebook cover, a print cover or both?
faq.a: An ebook needs only a front cover. A paperback or hardcover needs a full wrap: back cover, spine and front, sized for your printer and page count. Many packages offer both.

faq.q: When should I order the print cover?
faq.a: The spine width depends on the final page count and paper type. You can start the front cover early, but order the full wrap once the interior is finished and you know the exact page count.

faq.q: Can the designer use stock photos?
faq.a: Yes, if they are licensed for book covers and for the number of copies you plan to sell. Some licenses limit print runs. Ask for the license details for every image used.

faq.q: Should the cover follow genre trends?
faq.a: Usually yes. Readers look for signals of their favorite genre in color, fonts and imagery. A cover can be original and still clearly belong to its genre.
Confirm in writing that you may use the cover for the book, its marketing and future editions. Ask for the source file in case you need to change the text later.
